title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident describes a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI chatbot outputs by injecting large volumes of fabricated, strategically framed content into the information environment those systems draw on. The Hanover Institute, which had no legal existence and no named staff, published more than 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, using academic formatting and citations to simulate the appearance of credible scholarship. The goal was for that content to be ingested by AI systems and to shift how chatbots respond to questions about Israeli actions in Gaza.

The failure mode this exposes sits on the data side, not the model side. AI systems that synthesize information from web sources have no reliable mechanism for verifying that a source represents a genuine, independent institution rather than a shell created solely to seed their training or retrieval pipelines. The operation succeeded in altering some chatbot outputs according to the reporting, which means the manipulation reached the point of affecting system behavior. Catching it would have required source provenance checks, institutional verification, or detection of abnormal publication velocity, none of which are standard gatekeeping steps in most deployed retrieval or training pipelines.

What is not established is the full extent of which AI systems were affected, precisely how the altered outputs were measured, or whether any AI developers have since taken steps in response. The registration as a foreign agent is a documented fact, but the characterization of the broader campaign's scope and cost rests on a single report, and no judicial or regulatory finding has confirmed all details as stated.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words in nine days across 124 reports designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The website, which doesn't exist as a legal entity and has no named staff, presents pro-Israel arguments on controversial topics including allegations of genocide and war crimes in Gaza. The organization was registered with the U.S. Justice Department as a foreign agent working for the Israeli government through intermediaries, including European advertising group Havas Media. The reports use academic formatting and citations to appear credible while strategically framing information to minimize criticism of Israel.

The campaign is part of a larger Israeli government effort costing tens of millions of dollars to manipulate AI training data and chatbot responses. Israeli officials have privately expressed frustration about the campaign's failure to improve public opinion, which has significantly turned against Israel among Americans. Research shows the operation succeeded in altering some chatbot outputs, but failed to move polling numbers, indicating the underlying political issues rather than messaging are driving American attitudes about Israel.
